name.text: Find the mistake in a listed set

questiontext.text:
{@nm@} was asked to list \(C = {@rule@}\). {@nm@} wrote \(C = {@dset(shown)@}\).

(a) What is wrong with the list?

[[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]] [[feedback:prt1]]

(b) Write the correct list.

[[input:ans2]] [[validation:ans2]] [[feedback:prt2]]

generalfeedback.text:
Test each element of {@nm@}'s list, and each end value, against the rule \(C = {@rule@}\).

(a) {@why@}

(b) The correct list is \(C = {@dset(C)@}\).

questiondescription.text:
Sets: checking a listed set against its rule

Grade 12 CBE Core and Essential 1.1 (b): Find the mistake in a learner's listing of a set given in set-builder notation, and write the correct list.

Core and Essential

This question is original to this project.

INNODEMS CBC Grade 12 Mathematics, first draft by Ben Davies, 2026. Aligned to the KICD Senior School Curriculum Design, Core and Essential Mathematics Grade 12 (draft).

truefeedback.text: There is a mistake. Test each element of the list, and each end value, against the rule.

falsefeedback.text: That is not the mistake in this list. Read the rule again: which kind of number, and which ends are allowed?

truefeedback.text: Every element you listed belongs, but you have left out [[if test="is(nmiss=1)"]]1 element[[else]]{@nmiss@} elements[[/if]].
Your set contains every element it should, and also \({@dset(xtra)@}\), which [[if test="is(cardn(xtra)=1)"]]does[[else]]do[[/if]] not belong.

falsefeedback.text: \({@dset(xtra)@}\) [[if test="is(cardn(xtra)=1)"]]does[[else]]do[[/if]] not belong, and [[if test="is(nmiss=1)"]]1 element is[[else]]{@nmiss@} elements are[[/if]] missing. Start from the rule, not from {@nm@}'s list.

qtest.description: Said nothing is wrong; copied the list
Another mistake named; an element missing
